title: Policy-Mix VaR and Risk Budgeting

maps.tested: A genuine convergence: the handwritten sheet lists 'calculation of policy mix VaR' and an independent exam recall reports the exam asked for VaR by the policy-mix method. Two unrelated sources naming the same unusual construction is a strong signal.
maps.specifics: Reported verbatim: 'then VaR was asking to be calculated by policy mix method.' LO 88.e is the exact home: absolute, relative, policy-mix, active-management, funding and sponsor risk as a six-way sibling set. Also reported: '3-4 on portfolio return computation' and 'IR/2 active risk numerical'. Risk budgets across asset classes and active managers (LO 88.h) is the computational form.

vardeezReading: IM-6: Very Important; his note: "Suplus at Risk Calculation and LO 88.h - Risk Budegeting Calucaltions".

selectors.name: VaR by the policy-mix method
selectors.what: Policy-mix VaR = alpha x W x sqrt(sum_i sum_j wp_i wp_j sigma_i sigma_j rho_ij), using the policy weights on the benchmark volatilities and correlations, diversified. Also asked beside the asset VaR and the active-management VaR.
selectors.theory: Policy-mix risk is the risk of a passive strategy that follows the policy weights; the deviation of the current mix from policy belongs to active-management risk; the policy-mix and active VaRs do not add up to the asset VaR because of the cross-product term.

selectors.name: Six types of investment risk compared
selectors.what: Describe and tell apart absolute, relative, policy-mix, active-management, funding and sponsor risk: what each measures, which return or position it is computed on, and who bears it (funding risk on the surplus A - L; sponsor risk as cash-flow risk versus economic risk).

selectors.name: Expected excess return of a manager pool
selectors.what: Portfolio return computation for a pool of active managers: expected excess return mu_P = sum of x_i x mu_i, equal to IR_P x omega_P, from the managers' risk shares, expected excess returns or IRs and the portfolio TEV.
selectors.theory: Why the pool's expected excess return is the weighted sum of the managers' expected excess returns, and how it follows from the portfolio IR and the portfolio tracking-error volatility.

selectors.name: IR and active risk numerical
selectors.what: IR = mu / omega, with mu the expected excess return over the benchmark (Jorion's tracking error) and omega its volatility (TEV); solve for IR, mu or the active risk. Portfolio IR with independent managers = sqrt(sum of IR_i squared), not the sum or the average.
selectors.theory: What IR measures, why a portfolio of independent managers has an IR above any single manager's, and the law of active management (equal IRs give IR_P = IR x sqrt(N)).

selectors.name: Risk budgets across classes and managers
selectors.what: Individual risk budget for an asset class = alpha x sigma_i x w_i x W, summing to the undiversified VaR, which is at or above the fund VaR; two managers in one class combine as VaR = sqrt(V1^2 + V2^2 + 2 rho V1 V2); optimal relative risk budgets across active managers x_i omega_i = (IR_i / IR_P) x omega_P, with any slack in the index.
selectors.theory: Why the risk budgets sum to more than the diversified fund VaR, how a class budget is split between managers with correlation, and why the optimal relative risk budget is proportional to the manager's IR.

selectors.name: Surplus at risk calculation
selectors.what: Funding risk measured on the surplus S = A - L: surplus return R_S = R_asset - (L/A) x R_liabilities, surplus VaR = alpha x surplus volatility x A, and the expected surplus less that VaR to find the chance or size of a deficit.
selectors.theory: Why nominal liabilities act like a short position in a long-term bond, how falling rates can raise liabilities more than assets, and immunisation by matching asset and liability duration as the minimum-risk position.

notSelected: IM-6 a to d (the definition of risk budgeting, horizon, turnover and leverage on the buy and sell side, the investment process of large investors, hedge fund challenges), IM-6 f (VaR to monitor risk) and IM-6 g (VaR in investment guidelines, marginal and incremental VaR) carry no shape, no Map point and no Vardeez pointer.
